dossier.public_summary: The folded dip is driven by a single deep event and one very shallow event, so the depth is not repeatable. There is also a significant second eclipse about half the depth of the first, which points to a stellar eclipsing binary, not a planet.

reasons.why: Depths are not consistent: one transit is far too deep and one is effectively missing, p_consistent 2.375e-10. A planet should have repeatable depth; this scatter points to noise or a few bad events dominating the folded signal.
reasons.value: mean_depth_ppm 11508, chi2 47.77682467833705, dof 3, p_consistent 2.375546401166883e-10, outliers epoch 2 depth 383 sigma -5.4, epoch 0 depth 20474 sigma 4.3

reasons.why: A significant second dip at phase 0.3177 about 42% as deep as the primary with snr 5.521 well above the best brightening suggests an eclipsing binary rather than a planet. A planet would not show a secondary this deep.
